pictures.scene: Makovsky, A Boyar Wedding Feast — a vaulted hall crowded for a wedding, a white-bearded guest on his feet raising a gold beaker to the young couple while women in jewelled kokoshniks and long veils lean in, gold plate massed on a red-draped sideboard and a roast swan carried in at the left, once again, jesus spoke to them in parables, the kingdom of heaven is like a king who prepared a wedding banquet for his son

pictures.scene: Bonheur, Ploughing in the Nivernais — pale cream oxen yoked in pairs hauling a plough across freshly turned earth, a drover in a blue smock and wide straw hat walking beside them with a thin goad raised, broken clods filling the foreground under a lilac sky, he sent his servants to call those he had invited to the banquet, but they refused to come, again, he sent other servants and said, tell those who have been invited that i have prepared my dinner, my oxen and fattened cattle have been killed, and everything is ready, come to the wedding banquet

pictures.scene: Victors, The Greengrocer — a fruit stall on a cobbled street heaped with baskets of apples, pears, grapes, cherries and nuts, a woman in a rose skirt bending to taste one while a young woman in a plumed cap and an old woman in a black hood wait their turn, a laughing child and a boy with a spaniel at the front, but they paid no attention and went away, one to his field, another to his business, the rest seized his servants, mistreated them, and killed them

pictures.scene: Robert, Fire in Rome — a city burning at night seen through the span of a great stone bridge, flames roaring up behind the colonnades, a woman carrying a child up the river steps while people run along the quay, a seated statue standing black against the glare, the king was enraged, and he sent his troops to destroy those murderers and burn their city, then he said to his servants, the wedding banquet is ready, but those i invited were not worthy
pictures.name: pd_robert_fire_in_rome

pictures.scene: Bruegel, The Peasant Wedding — two servers carrying a plank door loaded with bowls of porridge into a barn, a man in a red cap passing the bowls along a crowded table, the bride sitting still beneath a green hanging cloth with a paper crown above her head while the guests eat and drink on every side, go therefore to the crossroads and invite to the banquet as many as you can find, so the servants went out into the streets and gathered everyone they could find, both evil and good, and the wedding hall was filled with guests

pictures.scene: Hemessen, The Unmerciful Servant — a man in a deep red gown with a gold brocade sleeve leaning low over an open money chest, one finger raised to his lips as he picks a gold coin from a sorted row, piles of silver and copper at his elbow and ledgers stacked on the shelf behind, but when the king came in to see the guests, he spotted a man who was not dressed in wedding clothes, friend, he asked, how did you get in here without wedding clothes, but the man was speechless
pictures.name: pd_hemessen_onbarmhartige_dienstknecht

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Saint Peter in Prison — an old prisoner sitting on the straw floor of a stone cell in a heavy brown robe, his hands folded in his lap and his head bowed, one shaft of light catching his white beard while the whole right side of the cell stays black, two iron keys lying on the straw beside him, then the king told the servants, tie him hand and foot, and throw him into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth, for many are called, but few are chosen

pictures.scene: Caravaggio, The Cardsharps — a young player in black velvet studying his cards over a carpeted table, an older man in a plumed hat and black striped sleeves leaning at his shoulder to read the hand and signalling with two gloved fingers behind his back, the accomplice reaching in from the right edge, then the pharisees went out and conspired to trap jesus in his words, they sent their disciples to him along with the herodians, teacher, they said, we know that you are honest and that you teach the way of god in accordance with the truth, you seek favor from no one, because you pay no attention to external appearance

pictures.scene: Brueghel, The Tax Collector's Office — villagers pressed into a wooden office with their hats held in their hands, a white-bearded man in a red jerkin at the front, another carrying a goose slung across his arm, a woman stooping with a basket of eggs, the walls hung with bulging document bags and shelves stuffed with bundled papers, so tell us what you think, is it lawful to pay taxes to caesar or not, but jesus knew their evil intent and said, you hypocrites, why are you testing me
pictures.name: pd_brueghel_tax_collectors_office

pictures.scene: Titian, The Tribute Money — Christ in a blue mantle over a rose robe turning calmly toward the questioner at the edge of the panel, whose bare arm reaches in from the left holding up a small gold coin between finger and thumb, show me the coin used for the tax, and they brought him a denarius, whose image is this, he asked, and whose inscription
pictures.name: pd_titian_the_tribute_money

pictures.scene: Panini, Interior of Saint Peter's in Rome — a vast basilica seen down the nave, a gilded coffered barrel vault overhead with painted banners hanging from it, the twisted bronze columns of the high altar canopy far off beneath the dome, small groups of visitors scattered across the marble floor, caesar's, they answered, so jesus told them, give to caesar what is caesar's, and to god what is god's, and when they heard this, they were amazed, so they left him and went away
pictures.name: pd_panini_interior_of_saint_peters_rome

pictures.scene: Philippe de Champaigne, Moses Presenting the Tablets of the Law — a white-bearded Moses in a blue mantle over gold brocade holding up the two stone tablets lettered with the commandments, rays of light springing like horns from his hair, a gold staff resting across his arm, that same day the sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to jesus and questioned him, teacher, they said, moses declared that if a man dies without having children, his brother is to marry the widow and raise up offspring for him
pictures.name: pd_de_champaigne_moses_presenting_the_tablets_of_the_law

pictures.scene: Van Dyck, Lord John Stuart and His Brother — two young brothers standing together on a stone stair, the elder in a gold doublet and broad lace collar leaning an elbow on the plinth, the younger in silver and blue satin with a silver cloak over his shoulder, gloves gathered in one hand, both in tall pale boots, now there were seven brothers among us, the first one married and died without having children, so he left his wife to his brother, the same thing happened to the second and third brothers, down to the seventh
pictures.name: pd_van_dyck_stuart_brothers

pictures.scene: Ancher, The Sick Girl — a young woman lying propped against a blue pillow in a yellow bed jacket, a black book slipping from her hand onto the white bedclothes, a red striped blanket folded along the foot of the bed, medicine bottles, a spoon and a jug of marigolds on the little table beside her, and last of all, the woman died, in the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be of the seven, for all of them were married to her

pictures.scene: Bouguereau, Song of the Angels — three angels in long white robes with tall pale wings bending close together to play, one drawing a bow across a violin, one holding a mandolin, a third pressing in at the edge, dark leaves behind them and the blue of the sleeping mother's robe at the corner, jesus answered, you are mistaken because you do not know the scriptures or the power of god, in the resurrection, people will neither marry nor be given in marriage, instead, they will be like the angels in heaven
pictures.name: pd_bouguereau_song_of_the_angels

pictures.scene: Flinck, Isaac Blessing Jacob — a blind old father sitting up in bed in a blue shirt under a fur-trimmed red robe, his white beard spread on his chest, one hand lifted over the head of the son kneeling at the bedside in a gold-braided jerkin, the mother watching from the shadow behind in a brown headcloth, but concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what god said to you, i am the god of abraham, the god of isaac, and the god of jacob, he is not the god of the dead, but of the living
pictures.name: pd_flinck_isaac_blessing_jacob

pictures.scene: Raphael, Saint Paul Preaching in Athens — a bearded apostle standing barefoot on a stone step with both hands flung up as he speaks, a green tunic under a rose mantle and a thin halo behind his head, a seated crowd in orange and red drapery below him listening and leaning toward each other, a colonnade and a domed rotunda beyond, when the crowds heard this, they were astonished at his teaching, and when the pharisees heard that jesus had silenced the sadducees, they themselves gathered together
pictures.name: pd_raphael_prediking

pictures.scene: Durer, Christ Among the Doctors — a boy with long auburn hair and a faint halo in a blue-green robe counting an argument off on his fingers, an old scholar pressed up against him open-mouthed with both bony hands raised in answer, other teachers crowding in at the edges with open books held up, one of them, an expert in the law, tested him with a question, teacher, which commandment is the greatest in the law
pictures.name: pd_durer_doctors

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, An Elderly Man in Prayer — an old man in a pale brown cloak with his eyes closed and his grey beard lit from the side, both worn hands pressed flat together in front of him above an open book lying on the table, the room behind him entirely dark, jesus declared, love the lord your god with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind, this is the first and greatest commandment
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_elderly_man_in_prayer

pictures.scene: Master of Alkmaar, The Seven Works of Mercy — a woman in a white apron and headcloth holding out a basket of round loaves at her own doorway while a townsman in a blue-green gown hands them on, a mother in green taking a loaf with a child reaching up at her side, a crippled beggar dragging himself forward on crutches across the cobbles, Christ standing quietly among the crowd, and the second is like it, love your neighbor as yourself, all the law and the prophets hang on these two commandments
pictures.name: pd_alkmaar_barmhartigheid

pictures.scene: Honthorst, King David Playing the Harp — a bearded king singing with his face turned up and his mouth open, a gold spiked crown set over a striped turban, an ermine-lined brocade robe clasped with a jewel at his breast, one hand laid along the carved frame of the harp beside him, while the pharisees were assembled, jesus questioned them, what do you think about the christ, whose son is he, david's, they answered
pictures.name: pd_honthorst_king_david_playing_the_harp

pictures.scene: Cefalu Cathedral, Christ Pantocrator — a gold-ground apse mosaic of Christ filling the curve of the vault, long hair falling past a cross-marked halo, a blue mantle over a gold tunic, the right hand raised in blessing and the left holding an open book of Greek letters, the Virgin standing below with her hands lifted between two winged archangels, jesus said to them, how then does david in the spirit call him lord, for he says, the lord said to my lord, sit at my right hand until i put your enemies under your feet
pictures.name: pd_master_of_cefalu_christ_pantocrator

pictures.scene: Brandon, A Scene in a Synagogue — a man in a pale fringed prayer shawl carrying the covered Torah scroll up a flight of carpeted steps, a boy below holding up the scroll's silver finials toward him, men in wide black hats and shawls waiting at the top, faces of children pressed over the balustrade in the dim hall behind, so if david calls him lord, how can he be david's son, no one was able to answer a word, and from that day on no one dared to question him any further
pictures.name: pd_brandon_scene_in_a_synagogue

lines.text: Once again, Jesus spoke to them in parables:
The kingdom of heaven is like a king who prepared a wedding banquet for his son.
He sent his servants to call those he had invited to the banquet, but they refused to come.

Again, he sent other servants and said, Tell those who have been invited that I have prepared my dinner. My oxen and fattened cattle have been killed, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding banquet.
But they paid no attention and went away, one to his field, another to his business.
The rest seized his servants, mistreated them, and killed them.
The king was enraged, and he sent his troops to destroy those murderers and burn their city.
Then he said to his servants, The wedding banquet is ready, but those I invited were not worthy.
Go therefore to the crossroads and invite to the banquet as many as you can find.
So the servants went out into the streets and gathered everyone they could find, both evil and good, and the wedding hall was filled with guests.
But when the king came in to see the guests, he spotted a man who was not dressed in wedding clothes.
Friend, he asked, how did you get in here without wedding clothes? But the man was speechless.
Then the king told the servants, Tie him hand and foot, and throw him into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
For many are called, but few are chosen.
Then the Pharisees went out and conspired to trap Jesus in His words.

They sent their disciples to Him along with the Herodians. Teacher, they said, we know that You are honest and that You teach the way of God in accordance with the truth. You seek favor from no one, because You pay no attention to external appearance.
So tell us what You think: Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not?
But Jesus knew their evil intent and said, You hypocrites, why are you testing Me?
Show Me the coin used for the tax. And they brought Him a denarius.
Whose image is this, He asked, and whose inscription?
Caesar's, they answered. So Jesus told them, Give to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's.
And when they heard this, they were amazed. So they left Him and went away.
That same day the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Jesus and questioned Him.
Teacher, they said, Moses declared that if a man dies without having children, his brother is to marry the widow and raise up offspring for him.
Now there were seven brothers among us. The first one married and died without having children. So he left his wife to his brother.
The same thing happened to the second and third brothers, down to the seventh.
And last of all, the woman died.
In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be of the seven? For all of them were married to her.
Jesus answered, You are mistaken because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God.
In the resurrection, people will neither marry nor be given in marriage. Instead, they will be like the angels in heaven.
But concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what God said to you:
I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? He is not the God of the dead, but of the living.
When the crowds heard this, they were astonished at His teaching.
And when the Pharisees heard that Jesus had silenced the Sadducees, they themselves gathered together.
One of them, an expert in the law, tested Him with a question:
Teacher, which commandment is the greatest in the Law?
Jesus declared, Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.
This is the first and greatest commandment.
And the second is like it: Love your neighbor as yourself.
All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments.
While the Pharisees were assembled, Jesus questioned them:
What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is He? David's, they answered.
Jesus said to them, How then does David in the Spirit call Him Lord? For he says:
The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.
So if David calls Him Lord, how can He be David's son?
No one was able to answer a word, and from that day on no one dared to question Him any further.
